Area.evidence_source: [/page/6/Text/4] Many informants described how they in their last conversation(s) with the deceased experienced the deceased as stuck in a problem situation. This was related to normal issues such as a break-up with partner, separation from childhood home and/or the experiences of being demoted or having failed at studies or work. It was, however, neither the problem in itself, nor the size of the problem that, in retrospect, was understood as a warning sign for a suicidal crisis. Rather, it was the perception of the deceased being stuck in a kind of irreversibility related to a mistaken decision, as if there were no way for them to get back on track.
